name: Enstrom 480 / 480B
summary: A five-seat turbine development of the 280 Shark: sleek and low-slung, used for patrol, training and corporate flying.

wings: Three-blade main rotor on a low mast
engines: Single turboshaft behind the cabin with a short exhaust stub
Smooth swept cowling, no tall stack
fuselage: Sleek swept canopy, long and low compared with the 280
tail: Slim tapering tail boom with a vertical fin
Horizontal stabilizer low on the boom and a two-blade tail rotor

tellTales: Sleek, low-slung turbine helicopter with a three-blade rotor
Long swept canopy and a slim tail boom
Single exhaust stub behind a lean cowling

confusedWith.howToTell: The 480 is larger and more streamlined, with a turbine exhaust and five seats; the 280 is a rounder three-seater with a piston engine.
The Bell 505 has a two-blade rotor and a blunt, boxy nose; the Enstrom 480 has three blades and a sleek swept canopy.
The MD 500 has an egg-shaped pod and a five-blade rotor; the Enstrom 480 has three blades and a long sleek canopy.
The H125 has a tall boxy cabin and a three-blade rotor on a taller mast; the 480 is lower and more swept, with a smaller cabin.
